title: Mass increase and acyclic cancellation for phase flows on quiver complexes
label: Stability and Geometric Degeneration · Paper 11

abstract_html: Trace-norm mass can increase along the Haiden–Katzarkov–Kontsevich–Pandit phase flow defined by positivity, giving a negative answer to the proposed mass-monotonicity question with the prescribed degree branches. For two-term complexes over a two-vertex parallel-arrow quiver, with degree-one term supported at the source and surjective source differential, we nevertheless prove quantitative acyclic cancellation. For fixed upper-half-plane charges, arbitrary surviving tuples and bounded initial arrow norms, a sufficiently large least acyclic singular value gives exponential comparison with instantaneous cohomology. The estimates allow unequal surviving dimensions and are independent of arrow count, stabilizers and acyclic condition numbers. The proof controls the polar phase using only the nonsingular cohomology block. For equal surviving dimensions and charges −1+i, 1+i, a finite infimum of the cohomology Kempf–Ness function forces its moment-map defects to tend to zero, without initial balance or attainment of the infimum. When the source differential is invertible, cancellation holds from every positive metric without a large-scale assumption, and the normalized cohomology metric converges. At fixed external differentials, static mass converges in C1 in bounded arrow coordinates. An explicit family converges in C2 while every positive Hölder seminorm of its Hessian diverges. An exact metric primitive also identifies a positive cohomology potential and a negative ambient Levi direction.
